title: Heading utilities were inert
lede: Chasing dead heading classes turned up the reason they were dead: the typography block in globals.css sits outside any @layer, so unlayered CSS outranks every Tailwind utility. 141 heading declarations across the app silently do nothing — and the public marketing hero was rendering at a third of its authored size.

stats.n: Authored text-8xl, was collapsing to the base scale
6 h1, 27 h2, 46 h3, 59 CardTitle, 3 dialog titles
Showroom only; the 141-site fix was deliberately not shipped
Login and support measured at 30px before and after

sections.heading: The public hero
sections.note: Captured from the real route at 1280×900, device scale 2. Nothing changed but the heading declarations in showroom-blocks.tsx.

pairs.title: /about
pairs.sub: Authored text-5xl sm:text-7xl lg:text-8xl with font-black and leading-[0.95].
pairs.beforeCap: Rendering at 30px, weight 800 — the base h1 scale. The headline reads as a body heading, and leading-[0.95] and text-balance have nothing to act on.
pairs.afterCap: 96px at weight 900, the size that was written. The tight leading and balanced wrap now do what they were for.

pairs.title: /about/features
pairs.sub: Same block, one breakpoint down at this width.

pairs.title: /support — deliberately unchanged
pairs.sub: Proof the fix is scoped and did not leak.
pairs.afterCap: Still 30px, weight 800. Its inert text-4xl was removed rather than activated, so the rendering is identical and the code no longer claims a size it never got.

changesNote: The root cause was diagnosed, measured, and then deliberately left unfixed. Only the demonstrable bug was shipped.

changes.h: The cascade, measured rather than assumed
changes.was: I had already written into the design language that heading utilities are dead code. That claim predicted the /about hero would render at 30px, which would look broken — so it was worth testing rather than trusting.
changes.now: Confirmed in the browser: on an h1, text-5xl, text-[32px], and a bare element all compute to 30px. The typography block opens after the @layer base block closes, and unlayered CSS outranks every layered rule. The claim held, and the hero really was broken.

changes.h: The public hero was fixed narrowly
changes.was: Five showroom headings carried authored sizes and weights that never applied.
changes.now: They use the Tailwind important modifier (text-5xl!, font-black!). Five call sites, zero effect anywhere else — verified by measuring /login and /support before and after.

changes.h: The correct architectural fix was measured and not shipped
changes.was: Moving the typography block into @layer base makes utilities behave normally and is the right structure.
changes.now: Tried, measured, reverted. It changes 141 headings at once — 59 CardTitles, 46 h3s, 27 h2s, 6 h1s, 3 dialog and sheet titles — most on authenticated surfaces that cannot be verified locally. Shipping that as a side effect of a heading cleanup would have been reckless. It is written up in docs/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md with the measurement and the impact count, and queued in the conformance checklist as its own slice.

changes.h: Inert declarations were removed rather than left to mislead
changes.was: /support, /privacy, and the 404 page carried text-4xl, text-2xl, and font-semibold on headings that ignored them.
changes.now: Removed. Seven declarations, all provably no-ops, so the rendering is byte-identical and the next reader is not misled into thinking the scale is set locally.

verification: Scope proof: /login and /support h1 measured at 30px/800 both before and after, confirming the showroom fix did not leak into the app shells.
Cascade proof: three synthetic h1 elements injected into the live page returned identical computed sizes, isolating the behaviour from any one page's markup.
notes: The 141-site fix is untested. It was applied, measured on three public routes, then reverted. No authenticated surface was checked while it was in place, which is exactly why it was not kept.
Only three public routes were captured. /about/tech-stack, /about/security, and /about/field-work share the same showroom blocks and were not individually captured.
Mobile widths were not captured. The showroom headings are responsive (text-5xl base, sm:text-7xl, lg:text-8xl); only the 1280px case was verified visually.

Related open item: Input and SelectTrigger are h-9 (36px), below the 40px target rule. FormCombobox was left at h-9 to stay aligned with them during the target sweep; raising all three together needs its own slice.
